title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to Grothendieck's sequel to 'La Longue Marche', in the part on the genus-1 / modular-group piece of the Teichmüller tower. There, 'G_3' and 'S_3' denote the symmetric group on 3 letters, ρ is an element of order 3 and σ one of order 2, with σρσ^{-1}=ρ^{-1}. The objects are extensions of (a twisted form of) S_3, and of S_3 times a 'cyclotomic' group, by an abelian group (scheme) M. These presumably encode the lifting of the elliptic elements of SL_2 to an abelianized fundamental group. The underlying problem is to choose rigid, Galois-compatible lifts of the two elliptic generators: the points with exceptional automorphisms, j=0 and j=1728.

Previous page (p. 704). A computation shows that a homomorphic section of G^+/μ_G over G_3 extends to a section over Φ_12^*×G_3 of G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G. This is formula (265): u(μ)=λ·u_μ, with λ=xλ_0+yλ_1 determined by (a_0,a_1,b). It yields Corollary (266): the restriction map Scindages(G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G over Φ_12^*×G_3) → Scindages(G^+/μ_G over G_3).

This page.
1. The map (266) is an isomorphism of sheaves on (Sch)/S. Since by the proposition of p. 702 the target is an M-torsor, the source is also an M-torsor via this isomorphism.
2. This translates into a statement about set-theoretic (abstract) extensions. In particular, over S=Spec(Ẑ), where the group schemes become profinite groups, the splittings of the extension G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G of Ẑ^*×S_3 by M̂ form an M̂-torsor. By restriction this torsor is isomorphic to the torsor of splittings of G^+/μ_G as an extension of S_3 by M̂. In other words, the arithmetic (cyclotomic Ẑ^*) part of the splitting is forced once the geometric S_3-part is chosen.
3. He begins a variant without dividing by μ_G={1,ω}. Here G^+ is an extension of H^+ by M, where H^+ is the central extension of S_3 by {1,ω}, i.e. the binary dihedral (dicyclic) group of order 12 with ρ^3=σ^2=ω.
4. Next page. Splittings correspond to pairs ρ'=ξρ, σ'=ησ with ξ,η∈M satisfying ρ'^3=σ'^2=ω and σ'ρ'σ'^{-1}=ρ'^{-1}. The argument that ω must go to ω uses the centralizer: Cent ∩ M = M^{S_3}. The conditions reduce to the norm conditions (1+ρ+ρ^2)ξ=0 and (1+σ)η=0, with general solution η=b(λ_1-λ_0).

This is a routine but careful nonabelian-cohomology computation: splittings of a split-by-abelian extension of a finite group, described by generators and relations, giving a Z^1 computed via norm equations.
errors: Calling the set of splittings an M-torsor (rather than a Z^1(S_3,M)-torsor) is valid only if H^1(S_3,M)=0 and M^{S_3} is trivial in the relevant quotient. Presumably this is established in the prop. of p. 702, after dividing by μ_G, but it cannot be checked from this page. The next page itself notes that M^{S_3} contains μ in the version without quotient.
Base S=Spec(Ẑ) is unusual notation (taking profinite points); the reading is uncertain from the handwriting.

ideas.what: Restriction from splittings over Ẑ^*×S_3 to splittings over S_3 is an isomorphism of torsors: the cyclotomic/Galois part of a section is determined by its geometric part.
ideas.modern_name: Galois-equivariant lifts of elliptic elements / rigidity of sections at orbifold points of M_{1,1} (GT-type normalization)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Drinfeld, Nakamura, Schneps et al. (GT and genus-1 Teichmüller tower, 1990s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and the role of points with extra automorphisms, but not this computation

ideas.what: Splittings of an extension of the binary dihedral group of order 12 by an abelian M, computed via norm equations (1+ρ+ρ^2)ξ=0 and (1+σ)η=0.
ideas.modern_name: Nonabelian H^1 / Z^1 for a dicyclic group; cohomology of SL_2(Z) torsion

missed.claim: This is an explicit scheme-theoretic (sheaf on Sch/S) treatment of the torsor of splittings for the S_3/binary-dihedral part of the genus-1 Teichmüller data, uniform over a base and specializing to Spec(Ẑ). It is a detail of the unpublished 'Longue Marche' sequel rather than a new result.
missed.quote: Les scindages de l'extension G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G de Ẑ^*×S_3 par M̂ forment un torseur sous M̂, isomorphe (par restriction) au torseur des scindages de l'ext. G^+/μ_G de S_3 par M̂
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's approach to normalizing the Galois action at j=0,1728, a point later handled in GT-theory for genus 1. It is of historical interest only.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine, carefully executed cohomological computation inside a known unpublished project. The ideas (Galois-compatible lifts at elliptic points) are known in spirit from later GT literature, and nothing here appears genuinely new.
transcription_corrections: 'Q_12^*' should read 'Φ_12^*' (consistent with the previous page).
'𝔖^{+1}/μ_𝔖' is likely 'G^+/μ_G' (underlined G, with a plausible +1 superscript); '𝔖^+' in the last lines is likely 'G^+'.
'via ce p[?] isomorphisme' is likely 'via cet isomorphisme'.
'𝔖_3' corresponds to underlined G_3 (the symmetric group S_3) written in script.
